The 10-K names no rival, so Commercial Vehicle Group (CVGI), Core Molding Technologies (CMT) and Park-Ohio (PKOH) read as a CONVENTION of the run, rival figures XBRL transcriptions with one CMT figure checked against its filed statement. **Q1 IN**, narrowly **[M2012-065]**, **[M2011-014]**, **[M1998-044]**: a contract metal fabricator whose economics are foreseeable in kind from nine years of filings. **Q2 OUT** **[M2011-015]**, **[M2005-020]**, **[L2007-004]**, **[M2013-052]**: material cost passed through, a "value-based pricing model" named only as an aim, work re-awarded by request for proposal every three to five years, Item 1A's rivals able to compete on price and customers able to insource; the position bought (Mid-States Aluminum $95.9M in 2023, Accu-Fab $140.5M in 2025), sales on the filer's own pro forma down 9.7% in 2025; manufacturing margin 12.2% to 9.9% as sales fell 6.0%; mean operating margin 2.3% and operating income on total assets 2.6% over the span, below CVGI, CMT and PKOH (2.9% and 5.9%, 3.7% and 5.4%, 4.0% and 4.9%), no widening in nine years; the 2026 data-center ramp written down as contrary evidence and not credited, no filed year showing it and H1 2026 operating income -$7.3M. Contamination declared by the analyst: a `Test Runs/` listing taken to check the run's paths, showing the file names of the other 2026-10-17 runs, none opened; the MTRX commit subjects and the AYI and ARCB folder names in the session context; a memory index line; nothing about MEC; none used. Commits c8089f90 (template), beb79294 (Step 0, Q1), c2dbfceb (Q2), df63a4b2 (close). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Citations: the analyst's `check_ids.py` PASS (34 ids); the dispatcher's `dispatcher_cite_check.py`, 20 quoted fragments beside an id, all in their rows: **no slip**. Four tracked peer XBRL dumps over 200 KB untracked by the dispatcher (2365caa7). check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) whether the change-for-the-better route to TOO HARD (NATURE) opens when the improvement exists only in guidance (read as not); (2) the serial-acquirer rule credits organic growth as the filer reports it, and this 10-K reports none; (3) trough to trough does not say whether both trough years count (both counted); (4) no tax rate is fixed for the after-tax interest add-back; (5) nothing says whether the proxy peer group is preferred when the 10-K names no rival. runs.narr: OUT at Q2 (Mayville Engineering Company, NYSE MEC; contract metal fabrication, extrusion, coating and assembly for commercial vehicle, construction, powersports, data center, agriculture and military OEMs). Q1 IN narrowly; Q2 OUT: no pricing power on the filer's own words (material passed through, work re-bid every three to five years, a value-based pricing model only an aim), the position bought (Mid-States Aluminum, Accu-Fab), pro forma sales down 9.7% in 2025, the lowest returns of a low-return field over the whole span (operating income 2.6% of total assets against CVGI, CMT and PKOH at 4.9% to 5.9%); the 2026 data-center ramp not credited. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: guidance, Adjusted EBITDA featured, deal-completion cash awards, buybacks at about $15.15. Computation beneath the stop: no-growth value $11.88 all-equity against $13.90, fair $4.04 all-equity ($7.39 equity-only), no case earning the floor; not armed. Framework gaps for the operator: change for the better in guidance only, organic growth the filer does not report, trough to trough, the tax rate on the interest add-back, the proxy peer group when the 10-K names no rival.
